item.title: Xi chairs groundbreaking China-Russia-U.S. summit with Putin, Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired a historic summit here with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump, marking the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state. At the summit, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the three leaders had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. Xi described the trilateral meeting as being of groundbreaking significance. He said peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos. Peace has been the enduring pursuit of humanity, Xi said, noting that the planet has experienced more than 10,000 wars and that more than 60 conflicts are still underway in various parts of the world. More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world, he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) RIGHT WAY FOR MAJOR COUNTRIES TO GET ALONG "Humanity, living in the same global village, is a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together," Xi said. "In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities. Their positive interaction is not optional, but a must." In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large, he said. Noting that transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, Xi said the world is not peaceful and testing times reveal responsibilities on one's shoulders. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. He said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. "On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another," Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. "The Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny." As the main victors of World War II, the three countries should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II, Xi said. According to the trilateral declaration, the three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. "Nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons," Xi said. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, and combine their respective strengths in resources, manufacturing and consumption to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. "Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go," Xi said, adding that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) POSITIVE, CONSTRUCTIVE AND FRUITFUL SUMMIT Putin said that the victory in World War II brought the three countries together. Safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities, while properly addressing hotspot issues serves their common interests, he added. Russia stands ready to work with China and the United States to promote free and open international trade, safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on artificial intelligence governance, Putin said. Trump said that the United States, China and Russia, as nuclear powers, bear a special and important responsibility for maintaining world peace and stability. Trump said the summit is a historic event of great importance, drawing global attention. He said the three countries should jointly prevent nuclear proliferation and avert the catastrophic consequences that nuclear weapons could bring to humanity. Noting that dialogue is essential to maintaining stability and achieving peace, Trump said all issues should be resolved through dialogue. He expressed hope that the three countries better protect the planet and make the future safer. The three heads of state also exchanged views on major international and regional issues, including the Ukraine crisis, nuclear non-proliferation, the situations in the Middle East and on the Korean Peninsula. Summarizing main consensus reached at the summit, Xi described the meeting as positive, constructive and fruitful, saying that the three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace. Xi said that the three countries remember their history of fighting side by side during World War II and stressed the need to cherish the hard-won peace. Major countries should take seriously the legitimate security concerns of all nations, he added. Dialogue and negotiation represent the right way to resolve differences, Xi said. "There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close." He stressed that cooperation is the only way to meet challenges, calling for stronger cooperation on the basis of common interests to advance peace and pursue win-win outcomes. "The seeds sown at today's summit will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit," Xi said, calling on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world.

item.title: China urges Japan to correct its remarks and actions on Taiwan question
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
China's Foreign Ministry on Friday urged Japan to correct its erroneous remarks and actions on the Taiwan question as soon as possible, stressing that Tokyo must honor its political commitments in both words and deeds. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a question from a reporter about Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's comments about Taiwan following the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday. Takaichi said Japan's basic position on the Taiwan question remained consistent with the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, and that the positioning of the four political documents between the two countries as the foundation of bilateral relations had not changed. In response, Guo said Japan's adherence to the four political documents between China and Japan was a political responsibility and legal obligation that it must fulfill. This commitment should be reflected not only in its statements but also in its actions, he added. "For Japan, the pressing task now is to correct its erroneous remarks and actions on the Taiwan question as soon as possible. What is important is to adopt a correct attitude toward historical issues, and what is fundamental is to develop a truly objective and rational understanding of China," Guo said.

item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new positioning of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and given it new meaning based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new positioning has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as by the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, the repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against safety risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should do the right thing and avoid major disruptions to China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, and both sides should maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. item.title: China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The following is the full text of the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, released on Thursday. China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The Russian and U.S. heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. 1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. 2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. 3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. 4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao) SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all. Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. "The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade. As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination. Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. "History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development. "By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said. The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said. According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development, Xi said. Noting that the Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. "This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific," he said. Looking ahead, as China's ties with the Asia-Pacific grow increasingly close, Xi said China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. The development blueprint is "an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world," he said. Xi said China will provide the global business community with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, as well as an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. He highlighted China's accelerating efforts to develop a big, open market and build a modern industrial system, pledging a more stable and predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Calling the Asia-Pacific business communities "pioneers of the global economy," he said they are "more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization." Leaders of APEC economies, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, attended the summit. Having previously hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings in 2001 and 2014, China is taking on the role of APEC host for the third time this year. It has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year and reached nearly 50 practical outcomes with other APEC economies in the economic and trade field.
